name: Phende Ling

location.address: Via dei Monti Lariani, 22010 Carate Urio (CO) — mountain trail on Monte Bisbino, near Rifugio Bugone / Rifugio Murelli

tradition: Tibetan Buddhist, non-sectarian Rimé approach within the Mahayana / Gelug-influenced lineage of Ghesce Ciampa Ghiatso and Kyabje Dagri Rinpoche
technique: Śamatha (calm-abiding) meditation; also lojong mind-training, mantra recitation, and contemplative study
teacherAccess: Resident monk Ven. Thupten Tharpa lives on site year-round and can be requested for a one-on-one interview during a retreat; he also leads periodic group courses and teachings, in person and online
retreatOptions: Mostly self-directed, silent individual retreats lasting from a few days to several weeks; occasional group courses and teachings (in person and online), such as a multi-month lojong mind-training programme
about: Phende Ling is a small Tibetan Buddhist hermitage run by the Phende Ling association (founded 2017) on Monte Bisbino above Lake Como, reached on foot via a mountain trail from Carate Urio near Rifugio Bugone. Once an alpine pasture at roughly 1,200 metres of altitude, the eco-renovated hermitage has 12 beds across three shared rooms, a spacious meditation hall, a communal room with a fireplace, and a terrace overlooking the lake. The resident teacher, Ven. Thupten Tharpa, a student of Ghesce Ciampa Ghiatso and Kyabje Dagri Rinpoche, lives there permanently and offers courses and retreats in the non-sectarian Rimé tradition endorsed by the 14th Dalai Lama. The core practice is śamatha (calm-abiding) meditation, and most stays are self-directed, silent individual retreats of a few days to several weeks, supplemented by periodic group courses and online teachings. Guests observe the five Buddhist precepts and noble silence, share a daily karma-yoga housekeeping period, and support the hermitage through dana (donations) rather than fixed fees, since the resident monk cannot personally accept payment for teaching.
schedule: Individual retreat day: 6am wake, 7am meditation/intention, 8am breakfast, 8:30am cleaning and karma-yoga assignments, 11:30am silent communal lunch, free afternoon for meditation/study, 5pm meditation, optional light supper (no formal dinner), 7pm closing meditation and dedication
cost: No fixed room rate; individual retreats are sustained through dana (voluntary donation), since the resident monk cannot accept direct payment. Joining organized courses/group retreats requires becoming an association member (30 EUR annual membership fee); a bed-linen rental is 5 EUR if needed. A multi-month online lojong course, for example, has a 100 EUR package fee for members.
foodNotes: Simple communal meals (silent lunch, light optional supper, no formal dinner) sustained largely by member and visitor food donations — seasonal fruit and vegetables, bread, goat's-milk yogurt and cheese, plant milk, jam, nuts, dried fruit, coffee and tea; no meat is mentioned in the hermitage's suggested-donation food list.
workNotes: Guests take part in daily karma yoga, a housekeeping period after breakfast to help clean and maintain the hermitage, which has no paid staff.
